result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers stick closely to the brief, state the 20-loaf minimum plainly, and avoid unsupported claims of being established, building credibility from checkable specifics instead. A is tighter: both pieces are ready to paste, and its two short notes point to the right next proof (naming real cafés) and flag the risk of printing the 6am promise. B adds 'baked by hand,' which the brief doesn't say, and buries its good copy under alternates and a long list of notes, well past the couple of lines the rubric allows. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers stick closely to the brief, avoid claims they can't back up, and state the 20-loaf minimum plainly. A adds 'baked by hand', which the brief never says, and surrounds the copy with alternate lines, a long list of why it works, and optional extras, which is far more than a couple of lines of notes. B is tighter and ready to paste, and its single note about 'before 6am' being a printed promise is genuinely useful.
